block.field: Step Index Markov hedge armed — Step Index 100, four ticks. An order-three Markov chain on the tick directions is projected over the whole contract (ties included, because a strict Rise/Fall loses on them) and the sixteen-expert ensemble reads the same tape; the bot buys the model's side as the main leg and covers it with a fraction-sized opposite leg, on every tick both models agree and the chain clears its tie ceiling, z and lift gates. Stake ladder: base stake x martingale multiplier, capped by max stake and abandoned after martingale steps losses. Take profit and stop loss are session brakes.

Markov hedge held this cycle — the gate that stopped it is printed above: a thin chain, a four-tick tie rate over the ceiling, a lean too weak for its own sample (z), no lift over the unconditional read, a negative modelled expected value, the ensemble naming the other side, the stake ladder over the balance percent or the remaining loss budget.

Step Index Markov hedge: the stake ladder reached its step limit and was abandoned — the next stake is the base stake again. The ladder is a recovery ladder, not a promise: on this shape it is paid for by the four-tick tie.
Step Index Markov hedge stopped — the take profit, the stop loss or the balance rule was reached. Open contracts still settle; restart the bot to begin a new session.
